text: Kestrelline Rail will build its new maintenance depot in Port Ansgar, the company said Tuesday, after selecting the coastal logistics hub over two rival sites. The €78 million project will occupy 14 hectares on the eastern freight corridor and is due to break ground in May, with commissioning planned for late 2027. Kestrelline said the depot will support 220 permanent jobs and allow faster turnaround for its intercity fleet, cutting routine servicing time by an estimated 18%. Chief operating officer Mirel Dane said the location gives the carrier direct access to the harbor rail spur and mainline yards. For the rail sector, the move underscores a broader push to place heavy maintenance closer to freight-linked city edges.
